output:
I found 10 households where an owner missed a 2025 RMD. Five are owners who rolled their 401(k) RMD into one IRA payment, and five are beneficiaries of inherited IRAs.

## Owners whose 401(k) RMD was paid from an IRA (5 households)

In each case the owner was born in 1952, so 2025 was their first RMD year and it was due by 1 April 2026. Each signed a form adding up the RMDs of their two IRAs and their former employer's 401(k), then took the whole amount from one IRA. Every payment matches that combined figure exactly. But IRA RMDs can only be combined with other IRAs. A 401(k) RMD has to come out of the 401(k) itself, and taking extra from an IRA doesn't count toward it. None of the five 401(k)s paid anything out. The shortfall in each case is the 401(k)'s own RMD: its 31 Dec 2024 balance (positions plus cash) divided by 26.5.

| Household | Owner | 401(k) | Combined payment from IRA | Shortfall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HH-0120 | Laila Udeh | SYN-01200004 | $45,492.56 (2026-03-03) | $12,582.44 |
| HH-0236 | Xavier Santangelo | SYN-02360004 | $40,687.96 (2025-10-13) | $10,955.88 |
| HH-0664 | Freya Chaudhry | SYN-06640004 | $37,447.15 (2025-10-20) | $11,019.74 |
| HH-0371 | Rosa Tamura | SYN-03710004 | $46,029.07 (2026-02-18) | $15,164.26 |
| HH-5271 | Teodoro Villanueva | SYN-52710004 | $44,202.50 (2025-12-04) | $12,729.96 |

HH-0989, HH-0637, HH-0410, HH-0555 and HH-5814 have the same set of accounts but took the 401(k) RMD separately from the plan, so they are fine.

## Inherited IRAs (5 households)

I'm reading "IRA owners" to include people who own an inherited IRA in their own name; drop these five if you meant only original owners. In each case the parent had already started RMDs before dying. The custodian confirmations in the CRM say so. That means annual RMDs apply during the 10-year period. IRS relief covered only 2021–2024, so the 2025 payment was due by 31 Dec 2025. None of these accounts paid anything out in 2025 or 2026.

| Household | Beneficiary | Account | Divisor | Shortfall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HH-0607 | Noor Santangelo | SYN-06070002 | 31.3 | $11,760.82 |
| HH-0842 | Ines Trevelyan | SYN-08420002 | 45.7 | $7,090.19 |
| HH-0466 | Zainab Aldana | SYN-04660002 | 30.5 | $15,068.66 |
| HH-0491 | Orla Jablonski | SYN-04910002 | 21.7 | $14,976.93 |
| HH-7126 | Samuel Adeyemi | SYN-71260002 | 35.2 | $10,757.24 |

The divisors come from the IRS Single Life Table at the beneficiary's age in the year after the death, minus one for each later year. That table isn't in the files; I used the published values, so check them before acting.

## Everyone else

- **Met:** HH-0168, 0222, 0445, 6590, 0414, 0782, 6047, 0642, 0885 and 0190 each took exactly the 31 Dec 2024 balance divided by the right Uniform Lifetime factor. Where a household also made a charitable distribution from the IRA, that counts toward the total.
- **No RMD yet:** In HH-0193, 8312, 0611 and 8865 the spouse who died in 2025 owned no IRA, and the surviving IRA owner was under 73.
- **10-year rule only:** HH-7683, 0330, 0571, 0716 and 0328 have inherited IRAs where the parent died before starting RMDs, so there is no annual RMD.

For each missed amount, the usual fix is to take it now and file Form 5329, either asking for the penalty to be waived or paying the reduced 10% excise tax for correcting promptly.

arguments:
You are helping an advisor at a small independent advisory firm. This folder holds the records of every client household of the firm as they stood on 15 April 2026, one folder per household under households/<household ID>/, each with the custodian's files (custodian/), the firm's portfolio system (portfolio/) and its CRM (crm/).

The advisor asks: which IRA owners in the book had a 2025 required minimum distribution, from any of their retirement accounts, that was not met?

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "found" if one or more owners did, "none_found" if none did, or "unresolved" if the files settle no household as found and leave some unresolved
- "households": one entry per household with such an owner, each as {"household_id": ..., "owner_id": the owner's person ID, "account_ids": the accounts the unmet distribution had to come from, "shortfall": the amount not taken, "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "unresolved": the households the files cannot settle, each as {"household_id": ..., "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "figures": every figure you relied on from the files, each as {"label": ..., "value": ..., "source": the file it came from, relative to this folder}, adding "computed": true to a figure you computed from them rather than read
- "explanation": two or three sentences
